what_happened: The .olean tree was fresh (no FormalSystem source newer than FormalSystem.olean; no guard holder), so the Section 0 compile record could be produced by a single foreground lake env lean on a scratch file importing FormalSystem instead of a detached lake build.

The RaySummary README states the run-layer phase-2 first lemma as stabilization 'in the deadline counter c', but a ladder state carries two counters (q, c, n) and Count hands a starting region the length n, so realized cells at idle states depend on n as well; the first statement had to be re-derived over the pair (c, n) from Count's definition. Recorded as a sharpening, not a contradiction.

The research report already carries the full six-record decomposition (statement shapes, typed edges, file_scope, depth, costability) and the filing mechanics (state-write.sh creation object, manage-topics.sh, validate-state.sh, hand-authored ROADMAP edit), so planning needed no re-derivation of any statement; the plan only sequences and sizes the report's Recommendations 1-5.

plan-format.md gates the '## Lean Challenge Statements' section on task_type lean4 ('present only when'), but this lean4-typed task has no theorem deliverable (it proves nothing). lean-challenge-snapshot.sh treats a present-but-empty section as a hard error (exit 71) and an absent section as the R2 fallback, which itself exits 71 when Goals carries no identifiers. Resolution: the plan omits the section entirely, records the reason in Decisions, and marks --compare inapplicable to this task. The format file does not state what a lean4 plan with zero Lean goals should do.

Phase 1 compile record (74 check/print lines importing FormalSystem) exited 0 with no unknown identifier on the first run, and the evidence-probe gate completed from a warm cache in under two minutes; no rebuild was needed since the .olean frontier was fresh.

The plan's covering check for the specs/** spec file, verify-deploy.sh --only-gate 3,4, SKIPs both gates in this deploy-consumer tree (doc-lint and task-reference lint apply only to the source store), so it exits 0 with 0 checks and verifies nothing about the new file; the compile record and probe gate remain the phase's real verification.

The Phase 3 records file was first written as the dotfile .successor-records.json, which the repository's gitignore excludes under task directories, so git-commit-scoped.sh refused the phase commit (path not in the index). Renamed to successor-records.json (tracked) and updated the two references; no content lost.

The plan's recommended defensive checkpoint before Phase 4, git-snapshot.sh --no-revert 757, exited 1 after printing only its mode line, with no reason line captured in the log; the working tree was not modified (no-revert mode) and filing proceeded without a snapshot. Likely cause: other sessions' dirty specs/** files outside this task's file_scope. Worth a look at the script's silent exit-1 path.

The plan's Phase 5 attestation names 'check-task-references.sh exits 0' as a criterion, but the repo-wide lint exits 1 with 198 pre-existing occurrences outside specs/ (Boneyard/** READMEs and similar), none in a file this task touched: git diff --name-only 84be907f1..HEAD -- . ':!specs/**' is empty and the working tree has no non-specs change. The attestation's substance holds; the lint's exit code is a pre-existing-debt signal, not a regression. Annotated on the plan item as altered.
